title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the opening pages of a section 'Modules des courbes elliptiques : théorie transcendante'. An elliptic curve over C is described as a pair (V = t_E, lattice Π ⊂ V). V is recovered as the real vector space Π⊗R, and the complex structure on E is a complex structure on that real plane. This page sets up the dictionary between complex structures on a real 2-dimensional V and complex lines L ⊂ V_C on which Re : L → V is an R-isomorphism, i.e. lines not defined over R. Such lines form P^1(C) − P^1(R), two copies of the upper half-plane; this is the period-domain description that leads to the transcendental moduli space.

(8) Direction L → structure. Given L with φ = Re|_L : L ≅ V, Grothendieck takes the complex structure on V that is the CONJUGATE of the transported one: u x = φ(−i φ^{-1}(x)) = −φ(i φ^{-1}(x)).

(9)–(11) Direction structure → L. Let V_c be V with the complex structure u. The identity V → V_c extends C-linearly to ψ : V_C → V_c, with ψ(x+iy) = x + uy.

(12) L' = Ker ψ = {x + i u x : x ∈ V}. Since u_C(x+iux) = −i(x+iux), L' is the (−i)-eigenspace of u, the 'V^{0,1}' part. Re : L' → V, x+iux ↦ x, is bijective and antilinear for u: Re(i z) = −u Re(z). So the structure obtained from L' by (8) is u again, and the two constructions are mutually inverse. The margin note says this conjugation convention is imposed by wanting the identification of V with a quotient, and by the holomorphic/antiholomorphic convention for forms.

(13) A second description is begun and continued on the next page. A complex structure on V is equivalent to the data of (1) a compact subgroup U ⊂ Aut_R(V) isomorphic to the circle group, whose action on V_C has exactly two eigenlines, and (2) a choice of one of its two elements of order 4, equivalently an orientation of V. The order-4 element is u, the rotation by +π/2.

All of this is standard linear algebra: Hodge decomposition of weight 1 on a rank-2 real space, or a Deligne-torus/U(1) action. It serves as preparation for describing the moduli of complex elliptic curves as GL_2(Z)\(P^1(C) − P^1(R)).
errors: The transcription's '−φ(iφ(x))' should read −φ(iφ^{-1}(x)); it is either a slip in the manuscript or a transcription error.

No mathematical errors. The claims that Ker ψ = {x+iux}, that Re is bijective on it, and that Re is antilinear all check out: x + u(ux) = 0, and Re(i(x+iux)) = −ux. The deliberate conjugation in (8) is exactly what makes the two constructions inverse to each other.

ideas.what: Complex structures on a real plane V correspond to complex lines L ⊂ V_C with L ∩ V = 0, i.e. L ⊕ L̄ = V_C; L is identified as the (−i)-eigenspace of u.
ideas.modern_name: Weight-1 Hodge structure / period domain P^1(C) − P^1(R) = H^±
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann, Hodge; standard in Griffiths' period domains, Deligne's Hodge theory)

ideas.what: A complex structure is equivalent to a circle subgroup U ⊂ GL(V) with two eigenlines on V_C plus a choice of order-4 element (an orientation).
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structure as a representation of the Deligne torus S restricted to U(1); complex structures as SO(2)-conjugates in GL_2(R)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely textbook linear algebra setting up the transcendental description of moduli of complex elliptic curves. The only distinctive feature is the explicit care about the conjugation/sign convention, which is pedagogically nice but not new.
transcription_corrections: (12): 'Kes ψ' is 'Ker ψ'. The crossed-out expression after 'i.e. y =' is a struck attempt; the final form is y = ux.
Under φ in the line after (12), the manuscript annotates z = x + iu(x).
(13) item 1: the reading 'U ≅ ℂ^1' is doubtful. It is likely 'U ⊂ Aut_R(V)' (a circle subgroup); the word 'maximal' is struck.
Struck lines after 'antilinéaire' mention L = L' = Ker ψ ⊂ V_C.
Bottom-left margin seems to read roughly 'unique sur V; alors V → V_c ... antilinéaire', referring to the antilinearity of Re : L → V_c.
